title: Single-phase seedless generation beats the two-phase ideas prompt under rollout search
hypothesis: The two-phase ideas prompt (designs first, then per-idea implementation, as in the gpt-6.1-sol baseline and the exploration lane) produces structures that rollout search rescues less often than the single-phase prompt, so the exploration lane should switch prompts.

prediction.against: two-phase per-idea seedless generation (ideas_system/ideas_user then one implementation) in the same block, under identical 24-candidate independent rollout search
prediction.rationale: D-013's side observation: single-phase structures reached 0.80-1.00 after search versus 0.00 for the two-phase baseline run's promotion set; 0.15 is the smallest gain that would justify switching the exploration lane's prompt. Generation-block paired means give the primary interval.

code_changes: scripts/compare_generation_modes.py (--research-mode phase-searchability: arms single_phase and two_phase, otherwise the seedless-searchability machinery)

falsified_by: The block-level paired 95% upper bound below +0.15 refutes the predicted margin; an interval spanning zero is inconclusive. Invalid slots score zero in both arms; untrained (step-0) differences are reported as secondary.

cost_estimate.breakdown: 8 structures x 2 search seeds x (24 x 10 probe + 50 confirmation) + 8 x 50 original confirmation = 5040; LLM: single-phase 1 call + <=1 correction, two-phase 1 design + 1 implementation + <=1 correction, x 4 blocks = <=20

approval.note: approved by advisor gpt-6.1-sol (consult call_00026, run_as_is) under the user's 2026-10-22 session delegation

controls.note: control is the two-phase per-idea generator (ideas prompt, then one implementation) in the same block, searched identically; the metric is already single-phase minus two-phase

result.notes: Four generation blocks (3040-3043), one gpt-6.1-sol structure per generator per block (all valid; one two-phase correction); 24-candidate independent rollout search under seeds 3044/3045, probe s3046 (10), confirmation s3047 (50). Single-phase minus two-phase after search: block-level +0.698 [+0.395, +1.000]; placement-level [+0.658, +0.737]. Single-phase won every block: searched success 0.44, 0.81, 1.00, 0.92 vs two-phase 0.00, 0.02, 0.32, 0.04. Untrained, single minus two +0.250 (single 0.00/0.00/0.10/0.90; two-phase 0.00 everywhere, matching the gpt-6.1-sol baseline run). Replicates D-013's side observation with fresh blocks. Caveats: four blocks; the single-phase prompt is the legacy initial prompt, so the difference bundles prompt wording with the design-then-implement split; 13 LLM calls (within the 20 estimate), 5040 episodes.

verdicts.reasoning: Single-phase minus two-phase seedless generation under identical 24-candidate rollout search is +0.698, block-level 95% [+0.395, +1.000] over four independent generation blocks, placement-level [+0.658, +0.737]. The predicted +0.15 is exceeded and the lower bound is well above it. Single-phase won every block (0.44-1.00 vs 0.00-0.32); two-phase structures scored 0.00 untrained, reproducing the gpt-6.1-sol baseline's failure. Caveat: the arms differ in prompt wording as well as the design/implementation split, so the effect is of the whole generator, not of phasing alone.
verdicts.next_experiment: Change the pipeline: make single-phase generation plus 24-candidate rollout search the exploration lane's default (keeping lineage via a minimal idea record), then rerun the end-to-end two-lane search against the current configuration on a fresh confirmation set.

verdicts.reasoning: The named two-phase control was measured under the same rollout-search protocol [logs/research/phase_searchability_s3040/run.json]. The primary paired_success_difference was +0.6975, with a generation-block 95% interval of [+0.3949, +1.0001], entirely above the predicted +0.15 margin [logs/research/phase_searchability_s3040/summary.json]. All four generation blocks favored single-phase, with differences ranging from +0.44 to +0.88 [logs/research/phase_searchability_s3040/summary.json]. This supports switching to the tested single-phase prompt bundle, but the pre-search difference of +0.25 means the result does not isolate greater search rescue as the cause [logs/research/phase_searchability_s3040/summary.json].
